Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes. In the following
cases the functor (<REF_0001>) is fully faithful:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is surjective and universally closed
(e.g., finite, integral, or proper),
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is surjective and universally open
(e.g., locally of finite presentation and flat, smooth, or etale),
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0004> is surjective, quasi-compact, and flat.
<STRUCT_0005>

This follows from Lemma <REF_0001>.
For example a closed surjective map of topological spaces
is submersive (Topology, Lemma
<REF_0002>).
Finite, integral, and proper morphisms are universally closed, see
Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0003> and
<REF_0004> and
Definition <REF_0005>.
On the other hand an open surjective map of topological spaces
is submersive (Topology, Lemma
<REF_0006>).
Flat locally finitely presented, smooth, and <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms are
universally open, see
Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0007>,
<REF_0008>, and
<REF_0009>.
The case of surjective, quasi-compact, flat morphisms follows
from Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0010>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
Let <MATH_0002> be a descent datum relative to <MATH_0003>
with <MATH_0004> <ACCENT_0001>tale. Let <MATH_0005> be an
open covering. Assume that
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> the pullback of the descent datum <MATH_0006>
to <MATH_0007> is effective,
<STRUCT_0003> the functor (<REF_0001>)
for <MATH_0008> is fully faithful, and
<STRUCT_0004> the functor (<REF_0002>)
for <MATH_0009>
is faithful.
<STRUCT_0005>
Then <MATH_0010> is effective.

(Recall that pullbacks of descent data are defined in
Descent, Definition <REF_0001>.)
Set <MATH_0001>. Denote <MATH_0002> the pullback
of <MATH_0003> to <MATH_0004>.
By assumption (1) we can find an <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism <MATH_0005>
which comes with an isomorphism <MATH_0006> compatible with
<MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008>. By assumption (2) we obtain isomorphisms
<MATH_0009>.
By assumption (3) these isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition
so that <MATH_0010> is a descend datum for the
Zariski covering <MATH_0011>. Then Descent, Lemma
<REF_0002>
(which is essentially just a reformulation of
Schemes, Section <REF_0003>)
tells us that there exists a morphism of schemes <MATH_0012>
and isomorphisms <MATH_0013> compatible
with <MATH_0014>. The isomorphisms <MATH_0015>
determine corresponding isomorphisms <MATH_0016>
which glue to a morphism <MATH_0017> compatible
with the canonical descent datum and <MATH_0018>.
